## Summary

The source page (`page.html`) had **no CSS at all** — no `<link>`, no `<style>`, no inline styles — just plain markup relying entirely on the browser's default user-agent stylesheet (confirmed via windtailor: `body` gets only the default 8px margin, `h1` only the default 32px/700-weight heading style, `p`/`div` only default block display).

**Key decisions:**
- **No styling layer added.** Since fidelity here means matching *unstyled* default rendering, I deliberately did **not** wire up Tailwind (its preflight reset would strip the default `body` margin and `h1` font sizing that make up the entire visual appearance of this page — that would have been a regression, not an improvement).
- **Componentization considered and rejected for one case:** red-twine flagged `.product-card` (4 occurrences) and `.badge` (2 occurrences) as repeated fragments. `.badge` is a clean, uniform repeat. `.product-card` scored lower confidence (0.65) because occurrences have two distinct tag shapes (with/without the badge span) — correctly a single component with an optional badge slot, not two unrelated things, so I kept it as one structural pattern in the markup rather than forcing artificial uniformity.
- **Images:** left as the original relative hotlink paths (`/product-1.jpg`, etc.) exactly as authored — there's no live origin to resolve them against in this local-fixture context, and inventing one would be fabrication, so both original and clone render identical broken-image placeholders.
- **Nothing flagged as unrecreatable** — this page had no canvas/video/iframe/JS-driven content requiring escalation.

**Fidelity check:** Screenshotted both at the same 1280×900 viewport (`original.png`, `clone-round1.png`), diffed with odiff — result was **0 changed pixels, exit code 0**, i.e. a pixel-perfect match on the first round. No further iteration was needed.
